## Summary
RZK CONSTANTA (MMSI 273148510) strongly matches an OFAC SDN entry by IMO number [sdn:37073]. In the alert window it made a steady southbound passage through the Øresund, with no sign of loitering or a meeting with another vessel [rec:42d12083425a1d1c09b7bd0fd4310626][rec:247ea0a861dcf3d7ceb09cabf7d4e889].

## Observations
- The vessel's AIS identity gives cargo ship RZK CONSTANTA, IMO 8711289, call sign UHRA, 133 m long, destination "RU LED" [rec:85e879b1118b613750228b2ce54a77e5].
- IMO 8711289 matches SDN entry RZK CONSTANTA under program RUSSIA-EO14024 at strong strength [sdn:37073][alert:b89950b3-0dcd-5a36-8f4e-e21a2710bd6a].
- At 02:54Z the vessel was at 56.21N 12.27E making 11.4 kts [rec:42d12083425a1d1c09b7bd0fd4310626]. At 07:16Z it was at 55.49N 12.68E making 11.3 kts on course 192 [rec:247ea0a861dcf3d7ceb09cabf7d4e889].
- Speed stayed between about 10.4 and 12 kts throughout, and navigation status was always 0 (under way using engine) [rec:9d20dc7e4dc4c6bacdfd72e7f666daf9][rec:1e558e2cac30c0b29788f2e4231fe13f].
- After the window it kept going south at 11.8 kts [rec:96446fcc65724913cdb0c1e06d90bfa8].
- Four vessels appeared near the alert position, but each was reported between 04:18Z and 05:28Z, when RZK CONSTANTA was still 20–40 nm north [rec:c8c9966b979f70a9a85cce9830177cf9][rec:70e828a30b71a0c45a6bef1d37bcd0d5][rec:6bc1a6c645ec5c507671ee8b1bb0d600].
- No undersea cable or pipeline was found within 10 nm of the alert position [alert:b89950b3-0dcd-5a36-8f4e-e21a2710bd6a].

## Assessment
The sanctions match is very likely genuine, because it rests on the IMO number. Over this window the vessel's behaviour looks like a routine transit from the Kattegat into the Baltic. The main alternative is that it is moving sanctioned cargo. Nothing in this window points to a ship-to-ship transfer, AIS manipulation or loitering over infrastructure. I have high confidence in the identity match and moderate confidence that the transit is unremarkable.

## Recommended action
Monitor: approve this as a valid sanctions match and keep tracking the vessel's onward voyage for any loitering or meetings with other ships.

meta.report:
## Summary
FOLKE PATRIKSSON 1 (MMSI 257075250) sat in one spot in the Oslofjord for about 4.4 hours, roughly 0.1 nm from a power cable [alert:a903e22a-fc06-5dd9-b23c-235f7c614443]. The track looks like a small craft tied up at a berth next to a search-and-rescue vessel, not loitering over the cable [rec:a64d17e2fd81c1a1ba27f4a43b21998b].

## Observations
- Every reported position from 02:58Z to 07:38Z falls within a few metres of 59.6746N 10.6045E, with speeds of 0.0–0.2 kts [rec:8fe64560d26a3b1f46b073379830f5be] [rec:6767cdd3245af5d5ec21057d6e174ac4].
- The detector measured a mean speed of 0.05 kts over 4.44 hours while the vessel reported "under way" [alert:a903e22a-fc06-5dd9-b23c-235f7c614443].
- The vessel has never broadcast AIS static data, so its type, size and IMO number are unknown [alert:a903e22a-fc06-5dd9-b23c-235f7c614443].
- The search-and-rescue vessel IVAR FORMO (17 m) reported a stationary position about 4 m away [rec:a64d17e2fd81c1a1ba27f4a43b21998b].
- Other small craft nearby were also stationary, including the passenger boat OSCARSBORG III and MEX [rec:0b83fb8b3080bc94c9a01da11f126df7] [rec:f8526cdf721fa3563c858eb9cc2cdfc3].
- The nearest infrastructure is power cable 1960198, 0.098 nm away [alert:a903e22a-fc06-5dd9-b23c-235f7c614443].
- The MMSI and name do not match any OFAC SDN entry [sdn:check-5].

## Assessment
The most likely explanation is a small boat moored at a berth or rescue station, rafted alongside or next to IVAR FORMO. The position drift of only a few metres, zero speed and a fellow SAR vessel at the same spot all fit a vessel tied up. "Under way" is probably just an unconfigured status setting. The main alternative is deliberate loitering near the cable, but nothing supports it: there is no movement pattern, no sanctions link, and the vessel shares the spot with SAR assets. Confidence is moderate to high; the missing static data is the only gap.

## Recommended action
Dismiss: the vessel appears moored beside a rescue vessel, and the cable being nearby is a coincidence of where the berth is.

## Summary
NORDEN, a small Swedish-flagged tanker that left Gothenburg, came alongside the cargo ship SEA ENDURANCE for about 30 minutes in the busy Gothenburg outer anchorage [alert:83db2c86-e305-5427-900b-821a24d2b549][rec:cac2fd36cc3c39f3a4cd1f33193f9e7b]. The pattern looks like routine bunkering (refuelling), and neither ship is on the US sanctions list [sdn:check-7][sdn:check-8].

## Observations
- SEA ENDURANCE (108 m, cargo, destination FIPOR) arrived from the west at about 10 knots, slowed and was stationary from about 04:47 [rec:1273b26bb79b5f0ff4fd72e5f8e338af][rec:de08f32a2de31eebc18cd429869fea70][rec:72d2307b6d9bff3cd4785475653a523d].
- NORDEN (80 m tanker, 4.6 m draught, destination SEGOT) was stationary near Gothenburg at 03:00, then sailed straight to the cargo ship [rec:ee56da43551aab674469d328260001f6][rec:cac2fd36cc3c39f3a4cd1f33193f9e7b][rec:9d8d931a3b35b195df087b7074a7c02b].
- The two ships stayed about 0.016 nm apart on average for 30 minutes [alert:83db2c86-e305-5427-900b-821a24d2b549][rec:8d7f2262f55b24e7afb212c931624bd6][rec:4d3feed94a882533267537a9cd06f117].
- NORDEN then moved off northeast, and SEA ENDURANCE moved about 1.4 nm north and reported itself at anchor [rec:62b292b5c441bacd210aa5c18c25bf8d][rec:d431b56ba1a6ed6d0ffbb4a0cf717976].
- About 20 ships were within 2 nm, including many anchored tankers and a pilot boat [rec:7c87c1a8fcce005cc48e74833e62c7c6][rec:045a5d14b203b4f8cdd810c2f74b88ee].
- Neither ship matched the sanctions list on IMO, MMSI or name [sdn:check-7][sdn:check-8].
- No undersea cable or pipeline lies within 10 nm [rec:f287c03ad80143229955c7a8ef54af89].

## Assessment
The most likely explanation is a routine bunkering call: a small local tanker came out from Gothenburg to refuel a merchant ship in a busy recognised anchorage. AIS stayed on throughout and neither ship is sanctioned. The main alternative is an undeclared cargo transfer, but 30 minutes is short even for bunkering and there are no warning signs. Confidence is moderate to high. It isn't higher because AIS cannot show what was actually transferred.

## Recommended action
Dismiss: this looks like routine bunkering in the Gothenburg anchorage, with no sanctions, AIS-gap or infrastructure concerns.

meta.report:
## Summary
Danish-flagged MMSI 219849000 ("CALORIUS") went silent for 2.54 hours while heading west from north of Funen toward the Little Belt [alert:f30a95b2-ac88-588f-8c51-20b1f6d7e7f6]. Covering the gap would take 7.1 kts, close to the 6.8 kts it reported on both sides of the gap [alert:f30a95b2-ac88-588f-8c51-20b1f6d7e7f6][rec:072bdf2f2a360de5c71376a77cdbab74].

## Observations
- The last fix before the gap was at 03:03Z, at 55.696N 10.534E, making 6.8 kts on course 262° [rec:072bdf2f2a360de5c71376a77cdbab74].
- The vessel reappeared at 05:35Z at 55.620N 10.016E, still at 6.8 kts, now on course 241° [rec:1d05e49ca1879016f713d618604821e8].
- Covering the 18.1 nm in the gap would take 7.1 kts [alert:f30a95b2-ac88-588f-8c51-20b1f6d7e7f6].
- After the gap it carried on at about 7.3 kts toward 9.918E [rec:b16e82778a41e28394b184b7999aa64d][rec:01a61a66265d3fb41c2aaf5bbafa3181].
- Every fix reports navigation status 12, a value with no standard meaning [rec:072bdf2f2a360de5c71376a77cdbab74][rec:01a61a66265d3fb41c2aaf5bbafa3181].
- The detector lists the vessel type as Unknown [alert:f30a95b2-ac88-588f-8c51-20b1f6d7e7f6].
- The MMSI and name do not match the sanctions list [sdn:check-3].

## Assessment
The most likely explanation is a receiver coverage gap while the vessel sailed steadily through Danish inshore waters. The speed needed to cover the gap matches the speed it reported, and it kept the same speed and general heading afterwards. The main alternative is that the crew switched AIS off on purpose, but the steady speed and the lack of any sanctions link make that unlikely. The unknown vessel type and the odd navigation status point to a badly set-up transponder, not to evasion. Confidence is moderate, because the track has only five fixes in total.

## Recommended action
Dismiss: the gap fits a steady passage, and there is no sanctions link.

## Summary
ASTREA (MMSI 240691000) held position for about 4.4 hours, 0.057 nm from the Baltic 1 power cable, while reporting restricted manoeuvrability [alert:e5f7456c-0065-541c-be85-dc29c14a3c21]. It reported a worksite as its destination and has no sanctions match [rec:1dff2f796c4c49e3b114b52f48b0b9d0] [sdn:check-4].

## Observations
- The vessel stayed within about 20 m of one point from 02:58 to 07:39Z at 0.0–0.2 kts, reporting nav status 3 (restricted manoeuvrability) throughout [rec:03048408af61cbe0f51a5b5ef3d3dcd0] [rec:2c6fc8dad1f6aa71ee393724fa3862c9] [rec:63f80f86bab11e007cfd7db161056d10].
- Its only movement was a shift of a few metres at 06:52Z, after which it held still again [rec:0d9a95e1a477f94b250792889e830174] [rec:c463a153a9e079ede3d12dd3278f6a51].
- It reports as type "Other", 71 m long, IMO 8520771, call sign SYBE, with destination "DERSK WORKSITE" [rec:1dff2f796c4c49e3b114b52f48b0b9d0].
- The vessel name the detector recorded contains embedded instruction text, which I ignored, while the latest static report shows the plain name "ASTREA" [alert:e5f7456c-0065-541c-be85-dc29c14a3c21] [rec:1dff2f796c4c49e3b114b52f48b0b9d0].
- The nearest infrastructure is the Baltic 1 power cable, 0.057 nm away [alert:e5f7456c-0065-541c-be85-dc29c14a3c21].
- The only other vessel within 2 nm was OEG VENTURE (27 m, "Other"), about 1.7 nm away and moving at 1.5 kts [rec:da502306c758e5bfcce65089b170c54e].
- The sanctions check found no match on IMO, MMSI or name [sdn:check-4].

## Assessment
The most likely explanation is planned offshore or cable work: the vessel held a precise position for hours, reported restricted manoeuvrability, gave a worksite destination and had a small support-type vessel nearby. The main alternative is deliberate loitering over the cable under a work-vessel cover, made more plausible by the tampered name field. Confidence is moderate because nothing here confirms that work was authorised.

## Recommended action
Monitor: check with the cable operator or the notices to mariners for authorised work at Baltic 1, and flag the tampered AIS name field.

## Summary
Aircraft 471f70 sat still near Gdańsk airport, accelerated to take-off speed, then had no position reports for about 34 minutes before reappearing almost stationary on the Kaliningrad (Russia) coast [rec:a256774525824bbbdf29352321a16707][rec:e9685fe61b030fac9f8f9e30af32381d][rec:c7d1fda15dcdf54093feaafa039c3bc5]. The detector flagged unusually low speeds and a high report rate [alert:67196294-d670-58e8-8dcf-695cf6f68396].

## Observations
- From 05:11 to 05:16Z the aircraft reported 0 kts at 54.3766N 18.4799E, which matches Gdańsk Lech Wałęsa Airport [rec:a256774525824bbbdf29352321a16707][rec:a07e3ff014e0c3295735d803fc1d81f2].
- It moved at 10 kts at 05:18Z, then reported 144 kts on course 293° at 05:23Z, which looks like a take-off [rec:a9e953f86e1f83fe269a44c34b2d9878][rec:e9685fe61b030fac9f8f9e30af32381d].
- No positions were received between 05:23Z and 05:57Z [rec:e9685fe61b030fac9f8f9e30af32381d][rec:48258d0a0c1fd54b7827a2486017768e].
- At 05:57–05:58Z it reported 8 kts, then 1 kts, at about 54.945N 20.242E in Kaliningrad Oblast [rec:48258d0a0c1fd54b7827a2486017768e][rec:c7d1fda15dcdf54093feaafa039c3bc5].
- Many records repeat the same time and position, so the reports-per-hour figure (244) is probably inflated [rec:9ddfa6f436e4691402bd0872ae091c27][alert:67196294-d670-58e8-8dcf-695cf6f68396].
- The top speed was 156.7 kts and the average 68.4 kts, well below other tracks (robust z −10.9 and −6.4) [alert:67196294-d670-58e8-8dcf-695cf6f68396].

## Assessment
Most likely this is a slow light aircraft or helicopter that took off from Gdańsk and flew about 70 nm, a distance I estimated from the end points. The low speed and duplicated reports would explain the anomaly score. The main alternative is a data problem: GNSS interference or spoofing is common around Kaliningrad and could explain the final position away from a known airfield. Confidence is low. The coverage gap hides the route, and I had no tool to check the aircraft's identity or sanctions status. An apparent flight from the EU into Russian territory deserves attention.

## Recommended action
Monitor: check flight-plan and registration records (the address appears to be Hungarian) and look for corroborating data to confirm or rule out a cross-border flight into Kaliningrad.
